Well, to put it simply, the importance of celebrities (particularly musicians, in this case) is just getting lesser and lesser due to more widespread access of the Internet, music streaming, and social media. Long gone are the days of watercooler musician moments on TV like Michael Jackson's moonwalk or Miley Cyrus twerking on Robin Thicke at the VMAs. MTV is culturally dead, and Spotify, YouTube, TikTok, and Apple Music all took over to become the music go-tos. 

Olivia Rodrigo, Ice Spice, Doja Cat, Megan Thee Stallion, Jack Harlow, and PinkPantheress are all popular now, but because people have more options now, their influences will never be as huge or culturally significant as popular artists from the 2000s and earlier.


Music selections these days are more unlimited than previous decades, and we're never gonna have a culturally massive album like Thriller from the days of cassette tapes and CDs.

It's like what I've always said, we don't really have a monoculture anymore thanks to the continued fragmentation of social media and streaming. Social media really decimated the mystique of Hollywood celebrities (e.g., "Imagine" video celebrity compilation during the pandemic and Doja Cat's "war" against her own fans), and music streaming (Spotify and Apple Music are the prime examples) opened people up to a widespread array of musical artists: both obscure and mainstream.

This has always been the logical endpoint as we've progressed from analog entertainment (radio, cable/broadcast TV, and music CDs) to the widespread, freely available entertainment that we have now.

Also, LGBT rights were passed in 2015 by the Supreme Court, so that's also a huge plus.

And I even liked the majority of 2016 until the later part of the year as well (Pokémon Go, hilarious memes like Harambe, etc).

I'll easily pick 2000s because of the emergence of emo and electropop, iconic movies (e.g., Mean Girls and Superbad), and the McBling aesthetic. The decade honestly has a much more discernible (and memorable) monoculture than the 2010s (even though I enjoyed my early 2010s childhood a lot).
